does: Crushes food in a mortar until it becomes a paste.

intro.what: Pounding uses a mortar and pestle to turn firm aromatics and leaves into a paste.
intro.why: It teaches you to combine crushing and grinding while adding ingredients in manageable stages.

how: Start with the hardest thing: garlic, with a little coarse salt to grip it.
Pound straight down to break it, then grind in circles against the wall of the mortar.
Add soft leaves a few at a time, and grind each lot to a paste before the next.
Work in oil or cheese last, a little at a time.

cues.text: A thick, glossy paste with no whole pieces of leaf.
The scent of garlic and basil rises sharply as they break down.

mistakes.mistake: Filling the mortar with leaves, which slide about and bruise without breaking down.
mistakes.fix: Add a few leaves at a time.

quiz.question: What is the aim when pounding garlic and leaves for a paste?
choices: Large leaves merely coated in oil.
A cohesive paste without whole leaf pieces.
Dry chopped pieces that remain separate.
quiz.because: Breaking and grinding the ingredients brings them together instead of only bruising intact leaves.

quiz.question: How should the pestle move after firm ingredients have been broken down?
choices: Tap only the loose top leaves.
Stir without pressing against the surface.
Grind in circles against the mortar wall.
quiz.because: Grinding against the wall continues breaking the ingredients after the initial downward crushing.

quiz.question: Which smell change accompanies breaking garlic and basil?
choices: Their scent rises sharply as they break down.
Their aroma disappears as soon as they are crushed.
Their aroma stays faint until oil is added.
quiz.because: Breaking the aromatics releases their scent into the mortar and surrounding air.

quiz.question: A full mortar of leaves slides around without becoming paste. What should change?
choices: Add all remaining leaves and press only on top.
Add leaves in smaller batches and grind each before adding more.
Pour in all the oil before breaking the leaves.
quiz.because: Smaller additions keep the pestle in contact with the leaves instead of letting an overfilled pile slide.
